newsitem.title: USA: USAir says will not accept Boeing 757s.
newsitem.headline: USAir says will not accept Boeing 757s.

text.p: UsAir Group Inc said it has informed Boeing Co and Rolls-Royce Plc it does not plan to accept delivery of eight Boeing 757-200 jets it has on firm order for delivery in 1998.

USAir said in a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it did not make a $3 million progress payment due on the order Nov. 1 and was notified last week by Boeing that the manufacturer considered it in default of the contract.
USAir said it was in talks with Boeing regarding the 757 order as well as orders for 40 Boeing 737 jets on order for delivery from 2003 to 2005.
Altogether the 48 jets would be worth $2.2 billion at current list prices.

Last week USAir announced its intention to buy at least 120 and up to 400 Airbus Industrie narrow-body jets to replace the company's current fleet, which includes Boeing, McDonnell Douglas and Fokker aircraft.
USAir executives told analysts this week they had no further interest in the single-aisle Boeing jets on order.
USAir has deferred the Boeing several times and said it had a written agreement from Boeing extending the scheduled delivery dates of the 757s to 1999 from 1998.
But Boeing has threatened for terminate the 757 deal "and might seek to exercise other remedies against USAir," the airlines said in its filing.
USAir reiterated that it is exploring alternatives for new wide-body aircraft to suport its goal of increased international operations.
